pr.title: rustc_mir_transform: Make DestinationPropagation stable for queries
pr.description:
By using `FxIndexMap` instead of `FxHashMap`, so that the order of visiting of locals is deterministic.

We also need to bless
`copy_propagation_arg.foo.DestinationPropagation.panic*.diff`. Do not review the diff of the diff. Instead look at the diff files before and after this commit. Both before and after this commit, 3 statements are replaced with nop. It's just that due to change in ordering, different statements are replaced. But the net result is the same. In other words, compare this diff (before fix):
* https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/090d5eac722000906cc00d991f2bf052b0e388c3/tests/mir-opt/dest-prop/copy_propagation_arg.foo.DestinationPropagation.panic-unwind.diff

With this diff (after fix):
* https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/f603babd63a607e155609dc0277806e559626ea0/tests/mir-opt/dest-prop/copy_propagation_arg.foo.DestinationPropagation.panic-unwind.diff

and you can see that both before and after the fix, we replace 3 statements with `nop`s.

I find it _slightly_ surprising that the test this PR affects did not previously fail spuriously due to the indeterminism of `FxHashMap`, but I guess in can be explained with the predictability of small `FxHashMap`s with `usize` (`Local`) keys, or something along those lines.

This should fix [this](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/119252#discussion_r1436101791) comment, but I wanted to make a separate PR for this fix for a simpler development and review process.

Part of https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/84447 which is E-help-wanted.

r? @cjgillot who is reviewer for the highly related PR https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/119252.
pr.author: Enselic

processing.reason: The PR is an ordering/determinism fix, not a semantic miscompile. DestinationPropagation's candidate and merge maps changed from FxHashMap to FxIndexMap so that the visitation order of locals is deterministic. The affected regression test `foo(mut x: u8) { x = dummy(x); }` has both before/after revisions replacing exactly three statements with `nop`; only the choice of which StorageLive/StorageDead/self-assignment statements are nopified differs. The remaining value assignments produce the same result (the PR states "the net result is the same"). Therefore no concrete input can make the reconstructed historical original and transformed functions produce different observable numeric/boolean/character values while both remaining defined under Miri. Any such value-difference pair would be an unrelated invented rewrite, not the transformation justified by this PR.

analysis.summary: DestinationPropagation used hash-ordered maps for candidate merge selection, making the pass's query output depend on iteration order. The fix switches candidates, reverse candidates, and selected merges to FxIndexMap, giving deterministic visiting/selection order. Existing MIR expectations changed which statements became nop, but the PR states the net result remained the same.
analysis.originalLogic: DestinationPropagation finds local-to-local copy candidates, filters them, then greedily selects a subset of merges. The selection loop iterates over the candidate map: `for (src, candidates) in candidates.c.iter()`. Previously `Allocations` stored `candidates` and `candidates_reverse` in `FxHashMap<Local, Vec<Local>>`, and the selected subset was `let mut merges = FxHashMap::default();`. `apply_merges` then rewrote the MIR using those selected merges.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: With FxHashMap, the order of visiting candidate locals was not deterministic. Since the pass greedily chooses merges while iterating candidates, different iteration orders could choose different merge edges. The historical behavior therefore sometimes replaced one set of statements with nops and sometimes another set. The PR explicitly notes this is ordering-only: "Both before and after this commit, 3 statements are replaced with nop. It's just that due to change in ordering, different statements are replaced. But the net result is the same." The incorrect transformation is thus nondeterministic merge selection/output, not a semantic miscompile of the test program.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR functions containing multiple local merge candidates for DestinationPropagation, especially competing/overlapping candidates where the greedy order of src locals affects which assignment is merged or propagated. The affected regression tests are tests/mir-opt/dest-prop/copy_propagation_arg.foo.DestinationPropagation.panic-abort.diff and ...panic-unwind.diff, where locals _1, _2, and _3 participate in copy/assignment chains around dummy(move _3) and _1 = move _2.
analysis.trigger: A function has at least two eligible DestinationPropagation merge candidates such that selecting a different candidate first can change which local/assignment is merged. The candidates are held in a hash map whose iteration order is not part of the pass contract, so query results can vary for the same input.
preconditions: DestinationPropagation is run on MIR with multiple copy-like local candidates.
Candidate collection and selected merges are stored in non-order-preserving FxHashMaps.
The pass selects merges greedily by iterating over candidates.c.iter().
The resulting MIR is used in a query/stable-output context where nondeterministic statement replacement is observable in MIR dumps.
pitfalls: Do not judge this change by simply diffing the old and new MIR diff files line by line; the PR warns: Do not review the diff of the diff.
A different set of nop statements does not by itself prove a wrong rewrite; compare the actual value assignments and net MIR semantics in each decoded revision.
Do not conflate this ordering fix with changing the number of merges: the PR says both revisions replace 3 statements with nop.
Check all order-sensitive maps consistently: candidates, reverse candidates, and selected merges. Changing only one map may leave nondeterminism.
The reported issue is query stability/determinism, not a demonstrated wrong runtime result for the affected test.
analysis.testStrategy: Use the existing MIR-opt tests under tests/mir-opt/dest-prop/, covering both panic-abort and panic-unwind. Compare the exact post-pass MIR in both files, not just the count of nops, and verify the value assignments correspond to the intended merge. Add a focused regression input with multiple mergeable locals/candidates where greedy order can choose different edges; assert that the DestinationPropagation output is stable across repeated invocations and against the blessed MIR. Keep both panic modes because the supplied expectations changed for both.
evidence: so that the order of visiting of locals is deterministic
Both before and after this commit, 3 statements are replaced with nop.
different statements are replaced. But the net result is the same.
